claim: The CAS feature's C++ implementation progressed through an E0 reachability PoC, an E1 `Cas::Store` core rewrite, an E2 journal/epoch GC design, an E3 root-local part-manifest GC redesign, and an E4 ack-floor, freshness-meta, and ref snapshot-plus-log design.
The first CAS feature commit was `33d1b55b3e9`, dated 2026-06-02.
The E1 structural swap introduced the incarnation-token backend model through `Cas::Backend` and `Cas::Store` and deleted the PoC GC, codec, and pool layer.
The E2 GC design used per-shard epoch compaction with a `gc/log` and `gc/snap` delta journal, build heartbeats, and a roots `_registry`; almost all of this design was later deleted.
The E3 GC redesign used root-local part manifests and source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, removed the registry, and added a shard-incarnation ABA guard.

The E4 GC and writer settlement uses a one-pass heartbeat ack-floor round, writer point-reads of freshness metadata instead of a `RetireView`, retired rows inside the snapshot run, and a ref snapshot plus append log instead of a mutable root-shard manifest.
The explicit namespace registry was removed by `644eb7c6ade`; namespace discovery now uses `LIST(cas/refs/)`.
The mutable per-(namespace, shard) root-shard manifest was removed by `318291fe5e5` and replaced with `CasRefSnapshotCodec`, `CasRefLogCodec`, and `CasRefIntake`.
The writer no longer synchronizes a retired view or writer-side ack floor; it point-reads an add-only freshness meta at promote and copy-forward.
Retired rows are represented as `kCondemned` sentinel rows inside the snapshot run rather than as a separate retired-list object.
Liveness and the `min_active` build-watermark floor are carried in one `MountLeaseKeeper` slot.
The writer mount fence is the monotone `writer_epoch` stored at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/epoch`, and a fencing failure is reported as a recoverable `MountFencedException`.
Blob keys contain a per-blob algorithm segment under `blobs/<algo>/…`; `cityHash128` and `xxh3-128` are supported and `sha256` is accepted but backlogged.
S3-native staging is opt-in and streams to staging before a capability-probed conditional server-side-copy promote, with fail-closed fallback to local scratch.
The `Cas*` core versus `ContentAddressed*` frontend naming split began at the E1 swap commit `7133ba900b1`.
An EBR or epoch GC core never existed in C++; EBR appears only in TLA+ and design documents, while the C++ path went directly from PoC reachability to the `Cas::Store` token model.
The live `writer_epoch` mount fence is distinct from the deleted E2 per-shard epoch-compaction layout.

The `GcSnapPersist` event value and `gc_snap_persist` string have only an enum declaration and string case, with no emitter or reader; persisted numeric ordinal compatibility must be checked before removal.
The Build event's `UInt64 round` field is written as zero at five `CasBuild.cpp` sites because round is no longer a writer concept; consumers must be checked before removing it.
`folded_cursor` remains load-bearing for part-manifest folding but is a vestigial zero only on the ref-intake path, where `snap_generation` and `snap_attempt` supersede it.
The `retired_refs` map described in `Core/CasGcFormats.h` may be stale after retired-in-snapshot; its live field and population must be verified before removal.
The `part_id` cookie in `ContentAddressedExchange.h` remains a reachable legacy compatibility field in the replicated-fetch exchange.
The P9 `GcSnap::forget` cascade was short-lived: `GcSnap::forget` and `GForget` were added by `3243c6aec96` and `03e11643db3`, then the `CasGcSnap` unit was deleted by `3526407f1b1` ten days later.
The GC-side ack-floor one-pass round is current, while the writer-side ack-floor and `RetireView` synchronization was deleted by `55b76af5998`; these are separate mechanisms.
The retired-list-to-snapshot-run transition landed in `37813b4ea75` as the seven-task retired-in-snapshot series T1–T7.
The legacy `{writer_epoch,build_sequence}` pair in `Core/CasManifestId.h` survives the snapshot-plus-log ref model and needs an architecture-store audit to determine whether it can be reduced.
The adaptive large-blob HEAD-before-PUT threshold `dedup_head_first_min_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB.
On the baseline novel write path, each novel blob uses one conditional `PUT` with `If-None-Match:*`.
On the optimized warm-cache write path, each cached dedup hit performs a `HEAD` and a per-hash `.meta` point-read `GET` instead of a body upload.
A stale dedup-cache hit falls through from `HEAD` 404 to a normal conditional `PUT`.
The ETag fix makes `WriteBufferFromS3` return the `PutObject` or `CompleteMultipartUpload` response ETag, eliminating the head-after-put `HEAD`.
`mutable_files` such as `txn_version.txt` are inlined into the root shard's `RootRef` protobuf and add zero S3 operations.
Each writer renewal uses one `PUT` carrying both the mount lease and the build watermark `min_active`, plus one `gc/state` `GET` for the current round.
Before the flat-combining queue, `casPut` conflicts measured 35% at `workers=2`, with each conflict costing one extra conditional `PUT` and one `GET`.
`Store::mutateShard` groups mutations for one `(namespace, shard)` into one read and one `casPut` per flush.
The shard-mutation queue achieved approximately 2.3× CAS-write compression and reduced intra-server conflicts from approximately 257k per hour to approximately 11 per hour.
The shipped factory default for `root_shards` is 32.
A cold `resolveRef` shard read costs one `HEAD` and one `GET`, while a warm single-flight resolution costs zero additional operations.
`shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` defaults to 200 and a value of 0 disables its TTL.
The shard decode TTL applies only to present entries; absence is never TTL-cached.
Strict-freshness callers such as the publish gate pass `allow_stale = false` and always issue a shard `HEAD` regardless of `shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms`.
A part-manifest open costs one manifest `HEAD` and zero or one `GET` depending on the `(ManifestId, token)` decode-cache result.
The generic `DownloadPart` path measured approximately 15 `HEAD`s and 15 `GET`s per replicated part.
The regular GC round is one pass consisting of a heartbeat ack floor, one `LIST` discovery sweep, a three-cursor fold, pre-CAS deletes, and one `gc/state` CAS.
The current regular GC round has request complexity O(delta) plus O(servers) and one `LIST` sweep, without an O(universe) GET or PUT phase.
The heartbeat floor phase costs one `LIST` of `gc/server-roots/`, N server-root `GET`s, and only rare token-guarded fence-out `PUT`s for expired mounts.
If a listed shard token matches the sealed folded token, GC skips the shard body `GET`; clamped-coverage shards are never skipped.
A newly condemned candidate receives one `HEAD` to capture its exact token, while an already-condemned entry is re-verified from the fold and is not re-HEADed.
Physical deletion is two-phase: condemnation is published first, then `delete_pending` is published, and the physical delete follows on a later round.
Snapshot-run consumers use one `HEAD`, one ranged tail `GET`, and one streaming body `GET`; a large footer may add one exact-footer ranged `GET`.
Snapshot-run streaming uses O(block) resident memory with a maximum current block size of 1 MiB, independent of run size.
A fully idle GC round with no journal changes and no retired entries performs zero run-object GETs and PUTs.
The remaining hot-pool snapshot byte-volume work is delta-runs plus periodic compaction, tracked as T1 and marked desirable.
The pre-P1/P2/P9 soak estimate was approximately 517 million read requests and 73 million write requests per day, costing approximately 571 dollars per day in request pricing.
In the 2026-07-19 post-fix chaos soak, a GC success round averaged approximately 5,305 GETs, 12,812 HEADs, and 4,156 DELETEs.
In the 2026-07-19 post-fix chaos soak, CAS-internal housekeeping issued 1,128,865 PUTs, dominated by one small `.meta` sidecar PUT alongside each real content blob PUT.
Read-only `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` performs a check-only startup probe, creates no GC or heartbeat thread, and throws a `READONLY` exception from mutating entry points.
Read-only CAS mode supports a WORM deployment with one writer server and multiple read-only mounters sharing the pool.
`clickhouse-disks ca-fsck --disk <ca_disk_name>` opens the CAS disk read-only, walks live refs and trees through the production read API, and enumerates the pool prefix with paginated `backend.list`.
`ca-fsck` classifies a live ref naming a missing object as `dangling`, which is an `INV-NO-LOSS` violation and the only hard reachability class.
Under the ack-floor pipeline, `pending-gc` and `awaiting-gc` present-but-unreferenced objects are expected transient classes rather than leaks.
A persistent `unaccounted` object outside the whole GC view is anomalous under INV-2, while an object created and dropped between rounds may be transiently `unaccounted`.
`ca-fsck` audits ref streams arithmetically using dense IDs `1..T` within `(namespace, writer_epoch)` and exact-key reads starting at `_ckpt.checkpoint`'s successor.
`unchecked` means the audit could prove neither a healthy frontier nor a broken chain; it is a coverage result that does not make the report unclean or exit nonzero.
A read-only `ca-fsck` records a per-namespace `CORRUPTED_DATA` failure and continues scanning other namespaces instead of stopping at the first damaged namespace.

`ca-fsck` exits nonzero for `dangling`, `chain_broken`, `corrupted_runs`, or `lifeless_keys`, but never exits nonzero solely for `stale_edge`; a zero exit code therefore does not prove a clean pool without checking `stale_edge`.
`ca-fsck --detail` adds tab-separated per-object rows, and `--timeout <seconds>` defaults to 600 seconds with 0 meaning unbounded.
`clickhouse-disks ca-gc-dryrun --disk <ca_disk_name>` is read-only and derives next-round delete candidates from `gc/snap` and `gc/state` without CAS writes or deletes.
The GC safety assertion is `{preview deletes} ⊆ {ca-fsck unreachable}`.
`ca-gc-dryrun` previews `zeroInDegree` only for target shard 0 when `gc_shards > 1`, so its oracle can miss candidates in other shards.

When `gc/state` is corrupted or missing a healthy adopted baseline, regular GC refuses every round, makes no further progress, and deletes nothing until `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` or `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild` is run.
Offline `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild [--force]` requires `<readonly>true</readonly>` and must never claim a live server's mount.
A GC rebuild reconstructs cursors and edges but reclaims nothing; blobs not named by a surviving manifest are retained as `unaccounted`.
A GC round emits one `Start` row and one `Finish` row in `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log`; a `Start` without a matching `Finish` indicates a hung or failed round.
Positive CAS scenarios must have no `Error` finish rows in `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log`; `NotALeader` rows on non-leaders are expected.
The `system.content_addressed_log` audit is enabled by default by the `<content_addressed_log>` configuration section and costs no rows or construction when no CAS disk is configured.
Positive scenarios assert that `system.content_addressed_log` contains no `read_missing`, `dangling_access`, `corrupt_dangle`, `corrupt_decode`, `snap_journal_incoherent`, or `exception` events.
A reclaim test must advance the ack between rounds because the deletion pipeline is condemn at K, `delete_pending` at K+1, and physical delete at K+2 when all acks are current.
A CAS health check should inspect correctness invariants and broad audit-log reasons before evaluating performance metrics.

`system.errors` counters can be high while matching `system.text_log` rows are sparse because `LogSeriesLimiter` suppresses repeated log lines; `last_error_message`, `last_error_trace`, and `system.query_log` `exception_code != 0` must be checked.
A legitimate CAS conditional-PUT collision can count as `S3_ERROR` or `PreconditionFailed` before being reclassified as `PutOutcome::PreconditionFailed`.
`system.blob_storage_log` does not log reads by default because `enable_blob_storage_log_for_read_operations` defaults to false and requires `enable_blob_storage_log`.
A CAS database used by the soak harness is created with `lazy_load_tables = 1` so transient startup recovery failures are retried on access instead of cached as terminal `FAILED` table-load errors.
`cas_request_budget.recovery_retry_budget_ms` defaults to 120 s for bounded recovery retries during CAS table startup.

The previously observed S01 memory bug was caused by `Build::putBlob` materializing a staged `BlobSource` into a `String`; streaming through `uploadFromSource` reduced a 2 GiB INSERT peak from 13 GiB to 4.33 GiB.

Concurrent explicit GC leaders could orphan blobs because a deposed leader wrote a final-key fold seal before losing the `gc/state` CAS; attempt-scoped generations keyed by `(gen, attempt = lease.seq)` fix this by hiding unadopted artifacts.
`listRootShardTokens` currently calls `backend.list` with `max_keys = 0`, re-enumerating the entire `roots/` prefix on every page and causing O(N²/1000) S3 LIST round-trips.
Ack-floor round soak validation is still required for a writer hard-killed during a commit burst, a paused writer holding the floor, and a request-count guard for O(delta)+O(servers) behavior.
A CAS MergeTree read routes inline entries to memory, blob-backed files to ranged S3 GETs, and verbatim files to plain `IObjectStorage::readObject` without CAS indirection.
The blob-backed read sequence is `resolveRef → readManifest → lookupPath → getBlobViewPlan → readBlobPayload → ReadBufferFromFileView`.
`resolveRef` hashes the ref name with `shardOf(ref_name)`, reads one root shard, and returns `std::nullopt` on a missing ref rather than throwing `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.
Manifest objects use the key shape `cas/manifests/<ns>/<writer_epoch>/<build_seq>/<ordinal>.proto`.
`readManifest` fails closed with `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` and `INV-NO-DANGLE` when a live ref names a missing manifest.
`readManifest` rejects a body whose self-described ref does not match the journal `ManifestRef` or whose `root_namespace_id` does not match the owning namespace with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
A blob location uses a key shaped as `blobs/<shard2>/<blobId>`, with a 256-byte `blob_header_len` offset for single-file blobs.
`readBlobPayload` issues a ranged read over `[0, offset + length)` and exposes only `[payload_offset, payload_end)` through `ReadBufferFromFileView`.
When a control object disappears between `HEAD` and `GET`, `Backend::get` returns `std::nullopt`; callers that require presence convert that absence to `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.
The CA-S3 lane's cacheless warm scan measured approximately three times local latency, 141 ms versus 47 ms, with 186 S3 GETs.
The CA disk has no local byte cache; its read-path caches cover shard and manifest metadata only, so repeated blob reads refetch bytes from the object store.
Column pruning is structural: the MergeTree reader requests only needed files, and CA performs per-file `lookupPath` and ranged reads.
`Placement::Inline` entries are served from decoded manifest memory through `ReadBufferFromOwnMemoryFile` with zero S3 operations.
A shard decode cache entry is keyed by the shard key and stores `{token, shard, validated_at}`; a token match means the decoded root shard remains valid.
Single-flight shard reads bound concurrent GETs for one shard to one, regardless of query concurrency.
The `(ManifestId, Token)` cache is safe because part manifests are immutable content-addressed objects, and a cache hit avoids a manifest `GET`.
B157 read-your-writes coherence increments `shard_write_seq[key]` before cache eviction and prevents a concurrent stale GET from re-caching an invalidated shard decode.

B115 was caused by `ReadBufferFromFileView` retaining a stale `file_offset_of_buffer_end` after remote `setReadUntilPosition` discarded its inner working buffer, which could produce duplicated and missing granules as wrong query results.

The B115 fix rebases `file_offset_of_buffer_end` from `impl->getPosition() + impl->available()` after every inner-buffer operation, including `next`, `seek`, `setReadUntilPosition`, and `setReadUntilEnd`.
B59 occurred because projection temp blobs were recorded in an open transaction without a committed ref, so committed-only `resolveRef` returned `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` during read-back.
The B59 in-flight overlay provides `tryGetInFlightStorageObjects`, `tryReadFileInFlight`, and `tryGetInFlightFileSize`, with inline staged bytes served by `ReadBufferFromOwnString`.
`hasInFlightDirectory(path)` returns true when staged entries have a `<proj>.proj/` prefix, allowing `loadProjections` to discover an in-flight projection through `existsDirectory`.
For committed projections, `existsDirectory("<uuid>/<part>/<proj>.proj")` checks for a manifest key with the `<proj>.proj/` prefix and `listDirectory` strips that prefix from child names.
After the all-tree part-files migration, `uuid.txt`, `txn_version.txt`, and `metadata_version.txt` are ordinary manifest entries and no longer populate `RootRef.mutable_files`.
Loose verbatim mountpoint objects use keys shaped as `roots/<server_root_id>/<path>` and are probed with a directory-safe `HEAD`.
Namespace-level verbatim files in the reserved `@cas@/_files/` segment are served from root-shard `_files`-keyed inline bytes and bypass the blob/manifest pipeline.

A live committed manifest ref structurally protects its referenced blobs from GC because the fold cannot mark them zero-in-degree, and deletion additionally waits through condemn and `delete_pending`.
The CAS-specific ephemeral reader pin for stateless or ref-less cross-node readers was only a design as of 2026-07-03 and is not implemented.
`Resolved::manifest_size` is always zero because `CasStore::resolveRef` never sets it; this is tracked as the minor B10 gap.
The replication `manifest_hash`-on-Keeper-znode idea B1 was rejected on 2026-07-14 because the manifest id travels in-band and replication remains disk-agnostic.
CAS backup requires bucket versioning to be off; versioning-suspended buckets are rejected as well.
With versioning disabled, CAS cannot use S3 CRR/SRR, AWS Backup for S3, S3 Object Lock, or Azure soft-delete and blob-versioning facilities that require versioning.
The current CAS safety model assumes one-live-object semantics; versioned-bucket marker stacks and version-specific conditional behavior are unmodeled.

The current backup scope can omit `gc/*` because GC state is rebuildable with `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` or `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild`; the durable data scope is `blobs/ + cas/ + roots/ + _pool_meta`.
A restored CAS pool can be recovered by mount, `fsck`, `ca-gc-rebuild`, and dropping dangling refs.
`FREEZE` creates per-part shadow refs under `shadow/<name>/…`; unchanged parts share blobs by hash and the refs act as GC reachability roots.

A proposed retention delay would defer GC graduation for R after condemnation, making recent states recoverable without copying data; a trash-prefix copy-and-delete alternative was rejected because S3 has no rename and would double writes.
Native `BACKUP TABLE … TO S3(...)` or `TO Disk(...)` reads CAS parts and writes plain MergeTree files, making it independent of the CAS format.
`allow_s3_native_copy` cannot optimize native `BACKUP` from CAS because a blob contains an envelope header and may use inline or shared placement, so raw `CopyObject` cannot produce file bytes.
A native `BACKUP` target on the same CA disk stores full-byte, non-content-addressed verbatim loose objects inside the CAS ownership domain and therefore is not an independent backup.
The chosen CAS-native backup is a second CAS pool receiving snapshot ref-sets and their hash closures, copying only destination-missing blobs with server-side `CopyObject`.

Within one pool, `BACKUP` is a per-disk snapshot, consolidation makes a selected snapshot pool-complete, mirror copies snapshots to a backup pool, fetch selectively pulls closures, and `RESTORE` relinks refs locally.
A CAS snapshot copies the table's current `_snap` body into `cas/refs/shadow/<name>/<table>@cas@/_snap/<txn>.proto` and adds one metadata object, while reusing the referenced part manifests.
Part-manifest cleanup must remain edge-driven by in-degree rather than namespace-prefix ownership because shadow snapshots can reference manifests under dropped table prefixes.

Frequent multi-disk snapshots are per-disk native snapshots, while consolidation asynchronously uploads hot-tier snapshot hardlinks through the ordinary write path and publishes a pool-complete shadow `_snap`.
Comparing hot snapshots through bare `checksums.txt` equality or filesystem inode witnesses was rejected; the CAS-native identity primitive is streaming re-hashing and pool-side deduplication.

The mirror daemon runs on the backup side, reads production with read-only credentials, writes with backup credentials, lists only `cas/refs/`, copies missing snapshot-closure objects, and never propagates deletions.
Mirroring pinned snapshot closures avoids a source GC race; a live-tail replicator holding a lease was rejected because it would add a GC-wedging actor.
The backup destination is a real CAS pool that runs standard GC over shadow namespaces, and `clickhouse-disks ca-fsck` verifies it.
No restore path writes to the backup pool; selective fetch copies a chosen snapshot closure into a fresh or living pool and local `RESTORE` republishes refs with zero data bytes.
A fresh pool mints its own owner and epoch, while imported manifests cannot collide with new ones because `ManifestId` includes the namespace.

The backup invariants are `BAK-RO` for no restore writes to backup, `BAK-EDGE-DRIVEN-MANIFESTS` for edge-only reclamation, `BAK-THIN-AFTER-MIRROR` for ordering, `BAK-INDEPENDENT-RETENTION` for destination retention, and `BAK-NO-IDENTITY-COPY` for identity objects.
The chosen backup design still needs a pool-level volume object, a v1 decision on consolidated-only versus partial snapshot mirroring, daemon packaging, snapshot metadata format, and RBAC details.
